_comment: Forbidden/parasite phrasing for The Friendship Practice, EN+FR. Adapted from a similar toolkit built for a different site — vocabulary rebuilt from scratch for this project's voice and content, not copy-pasted. Categories with 'scope: guides' are excluded from science-of-friendship.html and fr/science-amitie.html, whose hedging vocabulary (estimated/may/can/suggests) is deliberate and required, not a style defect.

self_referential.description: Phrases that describe the page instead of just being the page.

ai_tics.description: Generic LLM-sounding filler that doesn't belong in Carole's voice.
en: at the end of the day

audit_report_tics.description: Sounds like an analyst's memo, not an article. Does NOT include the page's own deliberate 'Source:' / 'En pratique:' / 'Ce que cela montre' pattern on the science pages, which is a designed structure, not a violation.

defensive_hedging.description: Undermines the brand's authority without adding accuracy. Different from the science pages' epistemic hedges (estimated/associated with/may/can), which stay.

vague_filler.description: Words that stand in for something concrete instead of naming it.

internal_jargon.description: Build-process or ops vocabulary that should never reach visible copy.

anglicisms_fr.description: Loanwords/calques to avoid in French copy. 'coach'/'challenge'/'tracker' are excluded: they are the established product vocabulary (coach amitié, défi, tracker), not accidental anglicisms.

placeholders.description: Text that should never ship. Does not match the intentional user-facing [bracket] fill-ins in the tracker's follow-up message templates.

weak_qualifiers.description: Verbal tics that just sound unsure, as opposed to the science pages' precise epistemic hedges. Advisory only, not auto-fixed: flag for a human read, since many hits will be fine in context.
